test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text:
Sodium oxide reacts with water to produce sodium hydroxide. 20.0 g of sodium oxide is dissolved in 500 mL of water. Neglecting the change in volume, the concentration of the resulting NaOH solution is _________ ×10-1M. (Nearest integer)
[Atomic mass : Na=23.0, O=16.0, H=1.0]

The Total pressure observed by mixing two liquid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo> </mo><mtext>and</mtext><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>350</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi><mo> </mo><mi>Hg</mi></math> when their mole fractions are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>and</mtext><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>3</mn></math> respectively. The Total pressure becomes<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>410</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi><mo> </mo><mi>Hg</mi></math> if the mole fractions are changed to<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>and</mtext><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn></math> respectively for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo> </mo><mtext>and</mtext><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>. The vapour pressure of pure <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mm</mi><mo> </mo><mi>Hg</mi></math>. (Nearest integer) Consider the liquids and solutions behave ideally

CO2 gas is bubbled through water during a soft drink manufacturing process at 298 K. If CO2 exerts a partial pressure of 0.835 bar then x m mol of CO2 would dissolve in 0.9 L of water. The value of x is _______. (Nearest integer)

(Henry's law constant for CO2 at 298 K is 1.67×103 bar)

The osmotic pressure of a dilute solution is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>7</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Pa</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>273</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>. Ferrous sulphate heptahydrate is used to fortify foods with iron. The amount (in grams) of the salt required to achieve 10ppm of iron in 100kg of wheat is ____________.
Atomic weight: Fe=55.85;S=32.00;O=16.00

The vapour pressure of 30% w/v, aqueous solution of glucose is ________ mm Hg at 25∘C.

[Given: The density of 30% w/v, aqueous solution of glucose is 1.2 g cm–3 and vapour pressure of pure water is 24 mm Hg.]

(Molar mass of glucose is 180 g mol–1)

At the same temperature, if one more mole of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> -heptane is added to this solution, the vapour pressure of the solution increases by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Hg</mi></math>. What is the vapour pressure in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mmHg</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></math> - heptane in its pure state______?

Given: At STP, molar volume of an ideal gas is 22.7L mol-1

[Assume 100% ionisation of the complex and CaCl2, coordination number of Cr as 6, and that all NH3 molecules are present inside the coordination sphere]
